A cropped heavy square hammer head descends from upper-left and touches a heated curved steel breastplate at the center. The handle exits the left edge. The breastplate fills the lower-right and continues beyond the frame, resting on a dark anvil whose top is cropped along the bottom. At contact, a short orange-white hot edge is being pressed smooth into the armor curve, with only two short ochre sparks. The plate is intact and being shaped, not shattered. Background is deep blue-gray with a broad muted rust-red sweep behind the contact.

Wide loaded flat-brush strokes follow the hammer descent and curved plate. Broad cool steel-gray strokes overlap warm umber underpainting, blunt dabs define the hammer planes, one broad hard shadow turns the armor. Keep the strongest small ivory-orange light at the hammer contact; sparse cream highlights elsewhere. Leave calm stretches of painted metal between broad directional strokes and retain uneven opaque endings. No etched detail or repeated tiny facets.

masterpiece, best quality, painterly, sketch, visible brush strokes, loose hand-painted texture, broken edges, blocky volume modeling.

A complete illustration with the freshness of a painted sketch, not an unfinished draft. Soft directional light reveals the planes of forms. Build volumes from confident planes of light and shadow with visible brush edges, while letting selected outer contours remain open. Use broad flowing paint masses, dry uneven strokes, and crisp small highlights appropriate to each material. Vary the brush size and edge sharpness between different materials. Preserve deliberate brush marks instead of smoothing every surface.
